gloss: somewhat low; on the low side; lowish

definitions.gloss: somewhat low; on the low side; lowish
definitions.explanation: Slightly or relatively low. The suffix め softens the adjective, indicating a tendency or moderate degree rather than an absolute quality.

examples.japanese: ⟦{温度|おんど}→温度：00333_ondo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{低|ひく}め⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{設定|せってい}→設定：04767_settei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Set the temperature on the low side.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{気温|きおん}→気温：00235_kion⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{低|ひく}めだ。
examples.english: Temperatures this summer are on the low side.

examples.japanese: ⟦{周|まわ}り→周り：01732_mawari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{聞|き}こえない→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、{低|ひく}め⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{話|はな}した→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。
examples.english: I spoke in a lowish voice so the people around us wouldn't hear.

notes:
Formed from ⟦{低|ひく}い→低い：02947_hikui⟧ (low) + the suffix め, which softens adjectives to mean "somewhat" or "on the ... side." This め pattern is extremely productive and commonly used in daily conversation to express preferences or approximate descriptions.

The め suffix attaches to the stem of i-adjectives (see RELATED WORDS).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {低|ひく}め⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{設定|せってい}→設定：04767_settei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to set on the low side
- {低|ひく}め⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{価格|かかく}→価格：00147_kakaku⟧: a somewhat low price
- {低|ひく}め⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{温度|おんど}→温度：00333_ondo⟧: a somewhat low temperature
- {低|ひく}め⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧: a lowered voice

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{高|たか}め→高め：14861_takame⟧: somewhat high
- ⟦{多|おお}め→多め：28421_oome⟧: somewhat more; generous portion
- ⟦{少|すく}なめ→少なめ：19120_sukuname⟧: somewhat less
- ⟦{早|はや}め→早め：11176_hayame⟧: somewhat early; on the early side

WATCH OUT:
{低|ひく}め (lowish) is not the verb {低|ひく}める (to lower): ⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{低|ひく}める means 'to lower one's voice', {低|ひく}め⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧ is 'a lowish voice'.
